context: Current closing price of Bristol-Myers Squibb (BMY): $58.80 USD as of 2026-11-20.
justification_text:
My point estimates across all three horizons reflect a relatively stable baseline with a modest upward drift. The 1-day estimate of 58.9 is anchored primarily to the most recent observed value, assuming mean-reverting behavior and no major imminent catalysts. The 1-week estimate nudges slightly higher to 59.1, reflecting a small positive trend momentum that I weighted into the forecast while acknowledging that short-term noise could easily dominate. The 1-month estimate of 59.5 continues that gentle upward trajectory, consistent with a mild bullish drift assumption baked into the baseline model, though the signal becomes increasingly diluted by uncertainty at that horizon.

Confidence interval widths expand predictably with time, reflecting the compounding of uncertainty across longer horizons. At 1 day, the 90% interval of roughly ±1.7 around the point estimate reflects typical intraday-to-next-day volatility, constrained by the high autocorrelation of prices at short horizons. By one week, the interval widens to roughly ±3.3, capturing the realistic range of weekly price movement under normal conditions. The 1-month interval of ±6.5 reflects the full accumulation of daily volatility over approximately 20 trading sessions, plus model uncertainty about whether the gentle upward trend will persist or revert.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside these intervals include macroeconomic data surprises — such as an unexpected inflation print or central bank policy shift — which could move prices sharply in either direction within hours, invalidating the 1-day interval. At the weekly and monthly horizons, geopolitical events, earnings surprises from major index constituents, or sudden shifts in credit market conditions could produce moves well outside the stated ranges. Liquidity events or technical breakdowns, such as a move through a key support or resistance level triggering cascading orders, represent tail risks that my intervals, by construction, only partially capture at the 90% confidence level.
